items.q: Explain to a non-engineer why a reverse-osmosis membrane needs pre-treatment.
items.a: RO membranes have extremely fine pores. Without pre-treatment, particles, hardness and chlorine foul, scale or chemically damage them, so output drops and membranes must be replaced early. Filters, softening or antiscalant, and carbon to remove chlorine protect them.

items.q: Summarise the trade-off between batch and continuous production in under 80 words.
items.a: Batch production is flexible: you can switch products easily, but changeovers cost time and unit costs are higher. Continuous production runs one product non-stop with low unit cost and steady quality, but it is expensive to set up and hard to change. Choose batch for variety and small volumes, continuous for high, stable demand.

items.q: Explain to a small-business owner why their website should not store customer passwords in plain text, and what to do instead.
items.a: If your databse is ever stolen, plain-text passwords give the thief every customer's pasword at once, and because most people reuse passwords, their email and bank accounts are at risk too. Store only a salted hash made with a slow algorithm like bcrypt or Argon2. A hash can't be turned back into the password, and the slowness makes guessing millions of passwords impractical, so a leak does far less damage.

Mentions that people reuse passwords on other sites
Recommends a slow password hash such as bcrypt, scrypt or Argon2, or a trusted login service
Explains why the recommended approach is safer

items.q: Explain to a junior developer what a Git merge conflict is and how to resolve it.
items.a: Git is a distributed version control system created in 2005, and it has become the standard tool in almost every software team, from tiny start-ups to the largest companies. Understanding how it stores history as a chain of commits helps a lot. Now, to the question. When you merge two branches and both of them changed the same lines of the same file, Git cannot know which version you want, so it stops and reports a merge conflict. It writes both versions into the file between markers like <<<<<<<, ======= and >>>>>>>. You open the file, decide what the final text should be, delete the markers, then run git add on the file and git commit (or git merge --continue) to finish. Many editors and IDEs have built-in tools that show both sides side by side, which can make this more comfortable, and there are also dedicated merge tools. With practice it becomes routine.
crit: Says a conflict happens when both branches changed the same lines, or one deleted what the other edited
Explains that Git marks the conflicting sections in the file (conflict markers)
Says to edit the file to keep the right content, then add and commit or continue the merge
Mentions testing or checking the result before committing

items.q: A recipe for 4 people uses 300 g pasta and 0.5 l cream. How much of each is needed for 6 people? Show the calculation.
items.a: Per person: 300 g / 4 = 75 g pasta and 500 ml / 4 = 125 ml cream. For 6 people: 75 x 6 = 450 g pasta and 125 x 6 = 750 ml cream.

items.q: Explain to a shop owner the difference between a '404 Not Found' and a '500 Internal Server Error' on their website, and what to do about each.
items.a: A 404 means the visitor asked for a page that doesn't exist, usually because of a broken or mistyped link. Find those links and fix them, or redirect the old address to the right page. A 500 means the server itself failed, often because of a bug or a broken plugin, so the page could not be produced at all. Ask your developer or hosting company to check the server's error logs.
crit: Says 404 means the page or address does not exist, for example a broken or mistyped link
Says 500 means something went wrong on the server or in the site's code
Suggests fixing or redirecting broken links for 404s
Suggests checking the server logs or contacting the developer or host for 500s

items.q: Explain to a shop owner the difference between a '404 Not Found' and a '500 Internal Server Error' on their website, and what to do about each.
items.a: A 404 means your server has crashed, so restart it. A 500 means a page was deleted, so restore it from a backup. According to Google, every 404 error lowers your search ranking by 37%.
